races.name: Newsells Park Stud Sweet Solera Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Harlequin Sky
runners_data.note: Jane Chapple-Hyam's filly has four runs of experience and has finished placed at Newmarket on Good ground before, but her form string of 3-5-3-6 shows she is finding winners ahead of her; a prominent run from De Sousa is likely but she needs rivals to do her a favour.
runners_data.comment: Harlequin Sky shaped with promise when third two starts back and returns here in good order just 14 days later, with experience over today's trip and going working in her favour; winless in her last four, she remains one to keep onside from stall two at 128 lb.

runners_data.name: Martinet
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's filly won over this exact course and distance last time on Good ground, and Prescott's patient placement record means she arrives cherry-ripe; as the lone front-runner she should enjoy an uncontested lead, and her fitness and trip-familiarity make her a genuine contender to last home.
runners_data.comment: Martinet won last time out and returns on a quick 15-day turnaround, with experience over today's trip and going in her favour — but rated 77 on our figures and ranked last of seven, she faces a stiff ask at the weights carrying 128 lb.

runners_data.name: Nuit d'Eclair
runners_data.note: Kevin Philippart De Foy's rapidly progressive filly won on Good ground over 6f at Newmarket last time and steps up to 7f for the first time here; David Egan takes the ride and she has the highest OR of the prominently-placed horses, making her the most credentialled tracker in the field.
runners_data.comment: Nuit d'Eclair arrives here on the back of a win one start back and returns to familiar distance and going conditions, making her a leading contender from stall five; the fourth last time out is the one blot to address.

runners_data.name: Sugar Yes Please
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's filly won over 6f on Good ground before finishing fourth, and her natural racing style is prominent — she is shown in midfield here only because the race cannot accommodate every front-biased horse; at 30 days between runs the fitness angle is worth monitoring, and her chance is tempered by the likelihood she won't get as close to the pace as she ideally wants.
runners_data.comment: Ranked sixth of seven on our figures, Sugar Yes Please faces a stiff ask despite winning last time out — that recent success is a plus, but her speed rating of 68 lags well behind the principals and gives little confidence she can bridge the gap today.

runners_data.name: Tie A Navyribbon
runners_data.note: William Stone's filly has a single run on her card — a third over 7f on Good ground — and an OR of 120 that makes her one of the two highest-rated runners; lightly raced and unexposed, her ceiling is genuinely unknown, but Josephine Gordon must thread a clean passage through traffic from an unproven tactical base.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out, Tie A Navyribbon has run over today's trip and going and comes here on a handy 22-day turnaround, though her rating of 81 ranks her fifth of seven and that speed figure suggests she may need to find more.

runners_data.name: China In Your Hand
runners_data.note: Charlie Fellowes has a recent 1-3 record over 7f on Good at Newmarket, and China In Your Hand is a natural prominent/tracking type whose competitive best comes closer to the pace than the hold-up slot she occupies in the map suggests; the style mismatch is a real handicap to her chance, though her course-and-distance win gives her a meaningful form claim if the race develops kindly.
runners_data.comment: China In Your Hand arrives on the back of a win last time out and has run over today's distance and going, giving her solid claims here; the main risk is that she rates only fourth of the seven on our figures, carrying 128 lb from stall 6.

runners_data.name: Graceful Song
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby's unbeaten filly won on debut over 7f on Good ground — exactly the conditions she faces today — and Billy Loughnane rides for the powerful Godolphin operation; she steps up in class sharply from a maiden but her profile is that of a horse with considerable upside, and she is one of the two horses most likely to lock in a prominent position behind Martinet.
runners_data.comment: Graceful Song comes into this on the back of a win last time out and has run over today's trip and going, giving her a solid profile at 128 lb from stall 3; the main risk is whether one recent start leaves her fitness an open question.

races.paceDynamic: Martinet is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with just six runners to navigate past from the gate, should secure a comfortable lead at her own pace on Good to Firm ground at Newmarket's July course. Graceful Song, Nuit d'Eclair, and Harlequin Sky are all prominent-style horses who will push to sit just behind her, creating a compact early shape rather than a true scorching gallop — sustainable fractions that suit a horse who can travel kindly and pick up off the bend. The field contains more genuine prominent types than the race topology can accommodate: Sugar Yes Please and China In Your Hand are both natural front-to-midfield racers redistributed in the map, with Nuit d'Eclair and Graceful Song — higher-rated, better-credentialed — most likely to actually lock in the prominent berths behind Martinet. This race shape — a measured, uncontested pace set by a single leader, with a tight prominent pack tracking — strongly favours a horse with a high cruising speed that can produce a decisive, sustained run from second or third position into the Dip, rather than a pure hold-up type relying on a strong late surge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Martinet Leads, Prominent Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Martinet bowls along uncontested and the race unfolds at a fair but unhurried pace, allowing a prominent tracker to reel her in from the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: Martinet sets a controlled fractions on the July course straight, giving the race a shape where horses travelling fluidly just off the pace can deploy their full cruising speed without needing an extraordinary turn of foot; the Dip and rising ground reward a runner with class and stamina over a pure sprinting burst.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Martinet Stays, Kicks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Martinet's controlled lead translates into a genuine front-running victory when rivals fail to close on the rising ground.
scenarios.body: Sir Mark Prescott's filly is fit from her recent 7f Newmarket win and Prescott's record of placing horses to win their grade is outstanding; if the prominent pack burns slightly too much fuel trying to close, Martinet's economy of effort keeps her clear.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Bunches, Hold-Up Lands
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group press Martinet harder than expected, creating a faster-than-anticipated pace that brings closers from deeper into the picture.
scenarios.body: China In Your Hand, though running out of its natural role in the map, does have a win over this course and distance and could benefit if the race dissolves into a tactical scramble; Tie A Navyribbon, lightly raced and unexposed, has residual each-way appeal if conditions produce a late surge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Upsets at Prices
scenarios.trigger: If Tie A Navyribbon's single run form line is significantly understated and she handles the step up in class with a peak performance.
scenarios.body: William Stone's filly is lightly raced with only a third on her card and an OR of 120 that looks incongruous against her sparse form, suggesting potential that is either well-founded or dangerously untested; if it is the former, a clean run in transit from Josephine Gordon could produce a shock.

watchPoints.text: Nuit d'Eclair and Graceful Song will both be fighting to track Martinet closely from the outset — if one gets a cleaner prominent berth than the other it could prove decisive, as neither will want to be further back than third at the two-furlong pole.

Martinet's ability to control her own fractions is central to the dominant scenario; if Graceful Song or Harlequin Sky presses her early and lifts the gallop beyond Martinet's comfort zone, the race shape flips and the front-runner's chance evaporates quickly.

Sugar Yes Please's 30-day absence is the longest freshen-up in the field — watch the market and paddock for signs of rustiness, as her redistribution to midfield already compromises her if she is not fully wound up.

Tie A Navyribbon's OR of 120 is conspicuously high for a filly with a single third-place finish; if that rating reflects private evidence from William Stone's yard, she could be significantly underestimated at a big price — monitor the morning market drift or support for an early signal.

races.name: William Hill Epic Boost Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Betty Boop
runners_data.note: Lone front-runner drawn low in stall 1, Richard Hughes has placed her patiently in a climb through the ratings; her two runs show she handles good ground well, but both came at shorter trips (5f-6f) and this 7f step up on the July course is an open stamina question — a style fit concern if she is swamped late.
runners_data.comment: Betty Boop arrives on the back of a win last time out and has experience of today's trip and conditions, making her a live threat at 131 lb from stall 5; the main risk is whether that weight anchors her late.

runners_data.name: Sanbona Warrior
runners_data.note: Won over this exact course-and-distance combination on good ground, which is a standout credential in this field; Marco Ghiani keeps the ride and the 21-day freshener from a silver medal over 7f at Sandown looks ideal preparation for a prominent racer with a clean trip in prospect.
runners_data.comment: Sanbona Warrior won last time out and was second two starts back, so he arrives in cracking nick after 21 days, though a rating of 77 ranking him sixth of eight suggests he faces a stiff task from stall seven at 128 lb.

runners_data.name: Rhodes Runner
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's two-year-olds routinely improve for this July course and the 7f trip; Rhodes Runner has placed at this distance before and Hector Crouch has strong course form, though three defeats since that placed run over 7f suggest he needs things to fall right rather than just the track suiting.
runners_data.comment: Consistent without a win in her last four starts, Rhodes Runner brings solid placed form — second and third in recent starts — and has run over today's trip and going before; drawn four and carrying 126 lb, the main risk is she finds a way to finish fourth again.

runners_data.name: Desert Legend
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon runner whose best efforts came at 5f-6f, and the 14-point blot in a 14-runner field last time raises questions; a genuine hold-up horse in natural style, he has been pushed into the midfield map because too many closers fill the rear — his true position will be off the pace and he needs a strong gallop he is unlikely to get here.
runners_data.comment: Desert Legend has shown flashes of consistency with a third last time out and a third three starts back, though the unplaced effort sandwiched between them gives pause. Fit on a 14-day turnaround with distance and going experience, he carries 124 lb yet remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Regal Tiger
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's juvenile is a natural prominent-running type with two second-place finishes at 6f on good ground, but with the prominent berths occupied he will be shuffled back from where he wants to be; that positional friction is a real tactical cost, and his soft-ground fourth suggests today's conditions are better, but getting race-position is the obstacle.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts despite back-to-back runner-up finishes, Regal Tiger has experience of today's trip and going but ranks seventh of eight on our figures — the consistency is there, the breakthrough isn't.

runners_data.name: Theheatison
runners_data.note: Nick Scholfield's 14-day string shows just two runners, muting trainer stats; the horse won over 6f on firm ground and has gone close at that trip, but his natural prominence is structurally blocked in this field and being forced to race in midfield — away from his comfort zone — is a meaningful negative in what will likely be a steady-paced contest.
runners_data.comment: Theheatison won two starts back but has finished fourth and fifth either side of that, and he ranks last on our figures here. Has run over today's trip and going, and 19 days since his latest run gives him a fitness case — but the overall profile makes him hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Mysterious Times
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby's operation is firing at 42% in the last 14 days, a strong stable angle, and Billy Loughnane partners a horse whose three runs have all produced placed efforts on good ground; the 29-day freshener and a step up to 7f could unlock more, though Mysterious Times has not yet won and needs a more searching gallop than Betty Boop is likely to supply.
runners_data.comment: Consistently placed in his last three starts — second last time out, and thirds in the two before that — Mysterious Times brings solid recent form into this, has run over today's trip and going, and 29 days between runs suggests he's fresh; the main risk is he's yet to win.

runners_data.name: Eabha
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's filly won most recently over 7f on good ground — matching today's conditions precisely — and Charles Bishop has the experience to manage a hold-up horse from the rear; the 30-day break is not concerning given the stable's hit rate, and she is the most natural closer in the field with a genuine winning profile at this trip.
runners_data.comment: Eabha arrives on the back of a win last time out, and with experience of both today's trip and going, she looks the one to beat here; a third two starts back and a third three starts back underpin her consistency, and 131 lb from stall three is the straightforward profile of a filly primed to follow up.

races.paceDynamic: Betty Boop is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to push her early, she is set to control this 7f contest at a sustainable, metronomic gallop on good-to-firm ground. Sanbona Warrior, Rhodes Runner, and the trio mapped to midfield — Regal Tiger, Theheatison, and Desert Legend — all carry prominent or hold-up traits, meaning the early order will be contested but Betty Boop is best placed to dictate from stall one without being seriously pressed. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than the map can accommodate at the head of affairs; of those, Sanbona Warrior and Rhodes Runner are most likely to actually secure their natural position behind Betty Boop, while Regal Tiger and Theheatison will be shuffled back from where they want to be. A controlled, single-paced gallop with a modest early tempo strongly favours prominent or just-off-the-pace runners who can travel in Betty Boop's slipstream and produce a sustained finish — held-up horses who need a truly searching pace to close ground are at a structural disadvantage here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Close Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Betty Boop dictates a steady-to-moderate gallop and the field settles into a rhythm with no serious pace injection until the final 2f.
scenarios.body: Betty Boop sets a comfortable tempo, and the runners just off the pace in the slipstream — Sanbona Warrior and Rhodes Runner — travel in ideal ground with energy in reserve for the Bunbury Mile straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough from the outset to string the field out and leave Betty Boop vulnerable inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Mysterious Times and Eabha, tracking from the rear with class held in reserve, benefit if honest fractions drain the front-runners; Eabha's recent winning form over 7f on good ground is directly relevant here.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Betty Boop Holds On Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Betty Boop produces a perfectly-judged front-running display and her pursuers use energy fighting for position behind her.
scenarios.body: The prominent rivals cannibalise each other mid-race leaving Betty Boop to steal a decisive break around the 3f pole; her good-going form profile and Richard Hughes's patient placement of a well-handicapped filly supports this.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaotic Finish
scenarios.trigger: If early jostling for prominent positions causes a fractured, uneven gallop that advantages a runner who bypasses the midfield squeeze entirely.
scenarios.body: Regal Tiger or Theheatison, both racing out of their natural position and hunting for a gap, could benefit from a disorganised race that resets the order late; however, their redistributed status makes this a low-confidence shape.

watchPoints.text: Betty Boop (stall 1) sets the entire race shape — if she jumps cleanly and establishes a lead of 2-3 lengths inside the first furlong, the pace narrative is locked in and hold-up horses face an uphill task.

Regal Tiger and Theheatison both want to race prominently and will jostle for position behind Betty Boop in the first 2f; watch for crowding around the 5f pole that could unsettle both and inadvertently create a pocket for hold-up horses to exploit late.

Mysterious Times is the highest-rated runner on OR=86 but has not converted three placed runs into a victory; if Billy Loughnane times the challenge to perfection under a weak early gallop, the class edge may not be enough to peg back the leaders — watch the market move as a guide to stable confidence.

Sanbona Warrior's course-and-distance winning form on good ground is the single most relevant form line in the race; if he secures a clean, uncontested passage in second or third, he will be the primary threat to any scenario where Betty Boop does not last home.

The going is described as Good throughout the July course card despite nominal "Good" overnight; watch for any official upgrade to Good To Firm before the race, which would marginally favour horses with firm-ground speed figures — Theheatison's best RPR came on Firm.

races.name: Tattersalls £40,000 EBF Newcomers' "Confined" Maiden Fillies' Stakes (For Horses Which Have Never Run) (GBB Race)
William Hill Extra Place Races Daily Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Morte Point
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on Good at this course in his last success and holds sound similar-going form; hold-up style means he needs Arctic Dawn to have done enough work to open the race up in the final furlong, and the 10-day turnaround under Ashley Lewis (3lb claim) keeps the weight manageable.
runners_data.comment: Morte Point landed a win three starts back but has since gone unplaced and sixth in his last two, leaving form hard to trust; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 10 days between runs suggests freshness, though 132 lb is no easy burden.

runners_data.name: Angel Hunter
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with six runs over 7f on Good including a second and fourth at this course and distance; Pat Dobbs provides experience but the form string of 667642 shows consistency without a win since joining Hannon, and he needs to find a gear he hasn't shown recently.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Angel Hunter does at least bring experience of today's trip and conditions, and that second last time out shows he retains ability — though his otherwise unplaced recent efforts make a win hard to envisage at present.

runners_data.name: Humam
runners_data.note: Raced prominently and placed twice over 7f on Good ground; stable has a mid-range 14-day strike rate of 4/34 and the tongue-tie is a note of interest, but a 26-length defeat last time over this trip is hard to ignore even allowing for that run being an outlier.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Humam showed a flash of form when third two runs back but has been unplaced either side of that effort; he has run over today's distance and going, and ten days since his last start leaves him acceptably fresh, though stall one and 128 lb are neutral factors for a gelding ranked seventh in this field.

runners_data.name: Kodi Lion
runners_data.note: Naturally wants to race prominently but this field has too many horses competing for that position — he is likely to find himself racing in midfield against his instincts; his best form at 7f on Good (a second at OR 87) came when able to stride on, and being denied that role blunts his chance here.
runners_data.comment: Kodi Lion has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 98 puts him among the most potent threats in the field — fifth two starts back and second five starts back hint at capability here. The worry is a winless recent run of five and a trainer yet to land a winner in 27 attempts this fortnight.

runners_data.name: Sword
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse on Good ground with a third at 7f in recent form; placed out of his natural rear position on the pace map, he will need a stronger-than-expected gallop to close on a well-organised leader, and the 7lb claimer Olivia Haines adds some uncertainty over the big-field Newmarket tactical read.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a third three starts back the lone bright spot in a largely disappointing recent sequence, Sword carries 125 lb from stall four and, while he has experience over today's trip and going, his rating of 90 leaves him hard to fancy against stronger rivals.

runners_data.name: Pinatubo's Legacy
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with a win from three starts but all prior form is on Standard artificial surfaces; this is her first run on turf Good to Firm and the jump to Newmarket from Southwell is a significant class and surface question — her true prominent style is squeezed out by this field's surplus of pace horses, compounding the unknowns.
runners_data.comment: Beaten out of the places last time out after a third and a win in the two starts before that, Pinatubo's Legacy has experience of today's trip and going in his favour, but ranked ninth of ten on our figures, he faces a stiff ask here.

runners_data.name: Castle Rock
runners_data.note: Two wins from three starts including a course and distance victory on Good ground, trained by Charlie Appleby whose yard is in solid 14-day form at 8/19; the 281-day absence is the one concern, but the horse is young, lightly raced, and the Appleby operation tends to have horses fit on return.
runners_data.comment: Castle Rock has winning form in his last three starts — back-to-back wins most recently — but 281 days off is a significant concern on return, and our figures rank him last of ten in this field. The distance experience offers some comfort, at least.

runners_data.name: Arctic Dawn
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter and highest-rated runner at OR 100 carrying 140lbs; won over this course and trip on Good ground and will set a controlled tempo, but the weight concession to every rival is significant and his STYLE_FIT flag notes he carries a mild discount in shapes where he is not able to dictate — here he can, which is his key asset.
runners_data.comment: Arctic Dawn won three starts back and was third four starts back, giving him a live profile over today's trip and going; the main risk is that his last two runs have been disappointing, and he'll need to bounce back sharply from stall 2 off 140 lb.

runners_data.name: Military Code
runners_data.note: All five recent runs have been over 5f on Good ground with consistent placed form; stepping up to 7f here is a significant test of stamina for a hold-up horse whose turn-of-foot looks geared to shorter, and the 7lb claim for Toby Moore is offset by the trip question — form does not obviously translate to this distance.
runners_data.comment: Twice runner-up in recent starts, Military Code arrives on the back of a strong profile — experience over today's trip and going, 133 lb from stall 10, and 28 days fresh — though he remains winless in his last five and must reverse his latest unplaced effort.

runners_data.name: Betty Clover
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose last five runs are all at 8f or above on Good or Soft; dropping to 7f is a slight shortening of trip, and the 52-day absence combined with no visible headgear change gives little reason to expect a sharp return — form has been modest with no win in recent starts.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Betty Clover nevertheless catches the eye as the top-rated runner here, and has run over today's trip and going before — a fourth two starts back hints at ability worth respecting, with 52 days since her last run.

races.paceDynamic: Arctic Dawn is the confirmed front-runner and, carrying top weight of 140lbs off OR 100, will set out to dictate from the front at a sustainable clip on Good to Firm ground at Newmarket's July course. With no genuine challenger for the lead — Angel Hunter, Humam, and Castle Rock are prominent types but none has the inclination to press a horse of Arctic Dawn's class to the front — the pace is likely to be honest rather than scorching, creating a rail-to-rail scenario where the leader controls tempo. The field carries a surplus of prominent and hold-up horses relative to the pace map's capacity: Kodi Lion and Pinatubo's Legacy are true prominent racers who will be shuffled into midfield against their natural instincts, while Sword is a genuine hold-up type also mapped out of position, meaning those three will be racing out of role. This scenario strongly favours horses who can travel close to the pace in the slipstream of Arctic Dawn and produce a sustained finish — prominent movers with class and Newmarket form are best placed, while true hold-up horses face a stamina test to close on a well-rated front-runner in control.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Arctic Dawn Controls, Held Up Beaten
scenarios.trigger: If Arctic Dawn dictates an uncontested lead and the pace is steady enough to leave closers with too much ground to make up.
scenarios.body: Arctic Dawn sets a measured pace from the front and the hold-up brigade — Morte Point, Military Code, Betty Clover — find themselves chasing a horse who has controlled every yard; on Newmarket's stiff finish, that deficit against a well-rated front-runner proving hard to close. The real beneficiaries are horses who travel prominently behind the leader and can quicken off the steady gallop — Castle Rock, Angel Hunter, and Humam are positioned to pounce in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Arctic Dawn's top weight tells in the final furlong and a prominent tracker dashes past on the run to the line.
scenarios.body: Arctic Dawn does the donkey work but the burden of 140lbs on Good to Firm ground catches up entering the final furlong, allowing a fresher prominent runner to collar the leader; Castle Rock, lightly raced and trained by Charlie Appleby with two wins already this season, is ideally placed for this shape. Angel Hunter and Humam, both prominent types with recent course and distance form, are also equipped to benefit from a tiring leader.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Suits Late Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Arctic Dawn goes faster than anticipated and burns off the prominent chasers, opening the door for a finishing burst from the rear.
scenarios.body: Should the early tempo be sharper than it looks on paper — perhaps with prominent types keen to challenge Arctic Dawn — the pace could compromise the midfield and create a stronger late finish for genuine hold-up horses; Military Code, whose form at 5f on Good ground is consistent, could benefit from the step up in trip if the race is run fast enough. Morte Point, a winner over 7f on Good ground, also carries claims if delivered late with a clear run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistribution Chaos, Wide Winner
scenarios.trigger: If the surplus of prominent horses ignites an uncharacteristically fast early pace that scrambles the whole field.
scenarios.body: With Kodi Lion and Pinatubo's Legacy both racing out of their natural prominent role in midfield, there is an outside chance their presence pushes horses forward and elevates the pace beyond Arctic Dawn's plan; in that scenario the race becomes genuinely messy and a horse like Sword, a true hold-up type who handles Good ground and stays 7f, could thread through late. This is the lowest-probability shape precisely because those horses are mapped out of position and are unlikely to dictate the tempo.

watchPoints.text: Arctic Dawn (top weight, lone front-runner) — watch whether he gets a truly uncontested lead from the outset; if Castle Rock or Angel Hunter push him harder than expected in the first two furlongs, the race shape changes materially.

Kodi Lion and Pinatubo's Legacy — both naturally prominent types forced into midfield roles; if either restores their position early by pushing forward, they elevate the pace and could compromise the chances of horses settled behind Arctic Dawn.

Castle Rock — 281 days off the track is a significant flag for a three-year-old; watch the market move and early paddock reports closely, as a flat or unready reappearance could remove the most obvious prominent beneficiary from contention.

Military Code — his entire form base is at 5f on Good ground; the step to 7f in a handicap where he is expected to come from behind is untested, and if the pace is steady he will have even more ground to make up than his hold-up style already demands.

Betty Clover — 52 days since last run, all recent form at 8f+, and dropping in trip; if she shows any signs of freshness or keen early behaviour, her hold-up style and the shape of this race become a poor combination.

races.name: William Hill Best Odds Guaranteed Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Runswick
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on good ground last time and arrives just 9 days later in excellent form — Billy Loughnane's booking for Ed Dunlop is a positive flag, and the hold-up style suits a genuinely run race; similar-going record of 4 from 8 with one win is solid.
runners_data.comment: Runswick shaped well when winning two starts back and was a close second three starts back, giving him a solid recent profile; he has run over today's trip and going, and nine days between runs suggests he arrives fresh enough to bounce back from a disappointing latest outing.

runners_data.name: Vincenzo Peruggia
runners_data.note: David Egan partners for Charlie Johnston who is 5/44 in the last 14 days, a moderate strike rate, but the horse placed on good-to-soft over 8f and handles the conditions; natural hold-up style will require a true pace, which this race should provide.
runners_data.comment: Vincenzo Peruggia has run over today's trip and going, arrives here just nine days after his last outing and is rated 91 by us, 4lb above his official mark of 87, suggesting there's ability to unlock — the risk is that he's been winless in his last five starts, including three unplaced efforts, and must prove his recent form has a ceiling worth trusting.

runners_data.name: Go Rimbaud
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with two wins on standard-to-fast turf for the Gosden yard; good-to-firm form is sparse (2 from 7 similar-going runs, no wins) and must fight Looka for the lead — the duel could cost him dearly late, though headgear (p) may sharpen focus.
runners_data.comment: Returned a winner two starts back but unplaced last time out puts him on watch; has run over today's trip and going, and 130 lb from stall 7 is the challenge if he's to bounce back at a nine-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Luzon Heights
runners_data.note: Placed twice over 8f on good ground and is the most consistent horse in the race on raw figures — a natural hold-up horse whose actual tactical role in this race will be constrained by the number of similar types, meaning he races with less freedom than his best form requires; the 29-day absence is not a concern given William Knight's patient approach.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked sixth of seven on our figures, Luzon Heights faces a stiff ask here, though he does bring distance and going experience and a second two starts back offers some encouragement; drawn in stall two carrying 124 lb.

runners_data.name: Drymee
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins over 8f on good and good-to-soft give Drymee legitimate claims on form — Ashley Lewis claims 3lb which helps the weights — but this is a horse who genuinely wants to race from off the pace, and with other hold-up types crowding the rear, finding clear daylight late on the straight course is a real challenge; 37 days off is within normal range.
runners_data.comment: Drymee arrives on the back of back-to-back wins and has experience of today's trip and conditions, but he ranks last of seven on our figures and his speed rating is only modest, making him hard to fancy despite that winning momentum.

runners_data.name: Looka
runners_data.note: The highest-rated runner in the field on OR 92 but returning from a 343-day absence — the big question mark — Silvestre De Sousa will look to use the rating advantage by dictating from the front; headgear (h) worn previously and likely worn again to sharpen focus; good-to-firm form limited to one win from three, all shorter than today's mile.
runners_data.comment: Looka landed a win two starts back and has run over today's trip, with his rating of 92 putting him right in contention from stall 5; the sole concern is a 343-day absence that leaves his fitness an open question.

runners_data.name: Man of Vision
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby's yard is in good form at 8/19 over 14 days and Toby Moore (7lb claimer) is a shrewd booking — the horse steps up from 6-7f to a mile for the first time, which is an open question, but has placed over 6f on good ground and the prominent style suits if the pace is honest; headgear worn.
runners_data.comment: Man of Vision brings solid claims here — a winner and a runner-up in recent starts, with experience of today's trip and going, and our rating just edges him to the head of the field. The risk is that his last two outings have yielded an unplaced run and a ninth.

races.paceDynamic: Looka and Go Rimbaud are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the gates, creating a genuinely competitive early gallop over Newmarket's straight mile on good-to-firm ground. Looka, returning from a 343-day absence under Silvestre De Sousa for Marco Botti, shapes as the likely pace-setter, but Go Rimbaud has winning form on similar surfaces and Robert Havlin will not concede the rail cheaply — the resulting duel will set an honest, pressure-filled tempo. Man of Vision sits prominent behind the front two, meaning the first three positions are occupied by forward-going types, which compresses the midfield and will leave the hold-up horses with more ground to make up in the straight. This field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all settle into their natural positions — Luzon Heights and Drymee are genuine hold-up horses pushed into a midfield mapping, but the pressure generated by Looka and Go Rimbaud means late finishers will need a truly run race to close, and the pace dynamic ultimately favours prominent-to-midfield runners who can sit just off the duel and pounce entering the Dip, rather than true closers who will face a stern task if the pace eases in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead Suits Stalkers
scenarios.trigger: If Looka and Go Rimbaud press each other hard from the start, setting a genuine end-to-end gallop.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners burn each other off, leaving a strong tempo that plays directly into the hands of prominent or mid-division horses who travel economically and pick up in the Dip. Man of Vision and Runswick, both with good-to-firm form, are ideally placed to benefit as the leaders tie each other up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Looka gets a soft lead and Go Rimbaud fails to challenge early, allowing a controlled, solo-set gallop.
scenarios.body: With Looka dictating a measured pace from the front, the race is run to suit the leader, who can conserve energy and sprint clear from two furlongs out. Go Rimbaud's good-to-firm form is limited but Looka's stamina on a fast surface is the key variable given the long absence.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Grinders Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuine but collapses in the final furlong, allowing the best horse in midfield to outstay all.
scenarios.body: A truly run race that ends with the leaders flattening out creates a window for the best-credentialed midfield horse to run through beaten rivals late. Vincenzo Peruggia has placed form at the trip on good ground and David Egan gives him tactical options.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is fierce enough to set up a sprint-finish from well off the pace for the true hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: Luzon Heights and Drymee are genuine hold-up types but are mapped out of their natural position in this race shape and face a significant challenge to find clear running from the rear on a flat, straight track. Even in the best-case scenario, they need the leaders to go very hard very early and the field to spread wide.

watchPoints.text: Looka (343-day absence) — if she shows signs of ring-rustiness in the early stages and fails to stride on, Go Rimbaud could inherit an uncontested lead and control the race entirely.
Man of Vision attempts a mile for the first time — if the step up in trip is too sharp he could stop quickly from a prominent position, taking other runners wide with him in the straight.

Looka and Go Rimbaud contesting the lead together — if the duel is fierce enough that neither has anything left entering the final furlong, the pace data suggests the winning time will be fast and the race could fall to whoever travels most economically in midfield.

Luzon Heights and Drymee — both genuine closers operating in a compressed midfield scenario; watch whether either finds a clear run down the centre of the track, as the straight Newmarket mile can get congested if the front group spreads wide.

Going officially Good To Firm for this race — fast enough that stamina will be tested at the mile trip, potentially exposing any runners whose best form is over shorter distances, particularly Looka and Man of Vision.

races.name: Keep Your Raceday Positive Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Merrimack
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Stuart Williams who won over this exact 5f course-and-distance on good ground recently; sim-going stats of 7/15 with a win and five places represent the best record in the field for this surface, and television headgear (hg:tv) suggests he is primed to concentrate — Chloe Lyons's 7lb claim is a meaningful weight relief on a horse already in competitive form.
runners_data.comment: Merrimack arrives in sharp nick after winning seven days ago, and has run over today's trip and going — third two starts back and a runner-up three starts back add further substance to his claims; the main risk is whether 138 lb blunts his momentum.

runners_data.name: Brave Nation
runners_data.note: Billy Loughnane takes over on this hold-up sprinter who has placed three times from five runs on good ground at 5f; Michael Attwater's yard is a tepid 1/14 in the last 14 days but the horse's own form figures of 3-3-4 in relevant conditions give him a realistic each-way angle if the pace truly collapses.
runners_data.comment: Brave Nation arrives here in decent nick on a 16-day turnaround, third last time out and with experience of today's trip and conditions; winless in his last five starts, though our rating of 84 marks him as the one to beat from stall 2 carrying 137 lb.

runners_data.name: Our Planet
runners_data.note: Hold-up type from Michael Keady's yard who has finished 6th, 7th, 4th, 6th across his last four runs — a pattern that screams consistency at the wrong end of the field; sim-going figures of only 5/11 with one win and one place offer little encouragement, and a headgear flag (hg:ht) hints at a trainer seeking solutions that have not yet materialised.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Our Planet nonetheless rates above his official mark and has experience of both today's trip and going — the main concern is that his recent finishes offer little reason for confidence.

runners_data.name: Thornaby Pearl
runners_data.note: Three wins from five runs on good ground at 5f make her comfortably the most in-form horse in this race on paper; she will front-run and can genuinely win from the lead if she avoids a speed duel, but an OR of only 67 means she is competitive in the handicap — apprentice rider Carmichael takes a further 7lb, and a last-run win eight days ago confirms she is at her peak.
runners_data.comment: Thornaby Pearl ranks bottom of the field on our figures and his speed rating of 63 offers little encouragement, making him hard to fancy despite an official mark of 67; that said, he boasts three wins in his last six starts, including back-to-back victories, and returns just eight days later in good heart.

runners_data.name: Lion's House
runners_data.note: Linda Perratt's horse is genuinely a hold-up type — his own hist shows he has settled off the pace in every recent run — but with five hold-up horses in a six-runner field he is mapped to midfield, meaning he will likely race closer to the pace than he wants; zero wins from 15 attempts on good going is a stark statistic, and a STYLE_FIT score of 0.92 signals his chance is materially reduced in a race where he cannot get his natural position.
runners_data.comment: Lion's House arrives 26 days fresh, has experience of today's trip and going, and our rating of 75 puts him ahead of his official mark — a second **five** starts back hints at the ability to threaten here; the risk is he's winless in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Loleeta
runners_data.note: A confirmed front-runner returning after an 87-day layoff, which is a significant concern in a sprint where sharpness from stall to stride matters; Stuart Williams's yard rate of 4/34 over 14 days is below par and her sim-going figures on turf are thin (1/8, no wins), so while she will push for the lead, her chance of sustaining the gallop on a first run back after nearly three months looks limited.
runners_data.comment: Loleeta has experience over today's trip and going, but a fifth last time out after 87 days off makes her hard to fancy, and her one win in recent starts came five starts back. Ranked fifth of six on our figures, she faces a stiff task.

races.paceDynamic: Loleeta and Thornaby Pearl are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the early lead over this 5f on good-to-firm ground at Newmarket's July course, creating a genuinely contested pace from the off rather than a controlled solo lead. Thornaby Pearl arrives in career-best form with three wins from her last five on similar going and will not easily surrender the rail, while Loleeta has been off 87 days and may be slightly less sharp early, but Stuart Williams's yard runs at 4/34 in the last 14 days suggesting managed expectations. The resulting honest gallop suits horses who can travel prominently without over-committing, as the pace will be genuine enough to stretch the field but not so suicidal that it gifts the race to hold-up types. Merrimack, a proven prominent racer with a win over this course-and-distance combination on similar going, is best positioned to exploit the front-running duel without being part of it. Note that Lion's House is a true hold-up horse redistributed to the midfield position on the map because this field carries more hold-up types than can all realistically settle at the rear; the prominence spots are already spoken for by Loleeta and Thornaby Pearl, and Merrimack will occupy the ground just behind them. The race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can sit just off the two pace-setters and pick up the pieces in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Duel, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Loleeta and Thornaby Pearl fight for the lead and set an honest gallop that stretches the field from the first furlong.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners burn each other up across the 5f trip, opening the door for a prominent horse travelling smoothly just behind to inherit the advantage inside the final furlong. Merrimack fits this profile precisely — a winner at this course on good ground who races prominently and has the tactical speed to capitalise on a pace-set race.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dominates Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Thornaby Pearl secures a clear lead from Loleeta and dictates a controlled enough gallop to see out the 5f strongly.
scenarios.body: Thornaby Pearl's exceptional recent form — three wins from five on good ground at 5f — makes her capable of winning even from the front if she gets a manageable lead; her rider Carmichael may attempt to produce a controlled front-running display rather than a flat-out duel. Her weight of 131lbs and OR of 67 gives her a viable handicap mark, and on this going she has already proven she can sprint clear.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace duel truly collapses the front-runners and leaves the door open for a late finisher to mop up.
scenarios.body: Brave Nation is the most credible hold-up threat here with an OR of 73 and a record that includes placed efforts on similar going, partnered by Billy Loughnane who is capable of producing a well-timed late challenge. Our Planet has the style but a poor recent record — six runs without a win since a novice success — and sim-going figures offer little confidence, making Brave Nation the more likely beneficiary of this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Mover Splits Field
scenarios.trigger: If the race develops into a compressed mid-race bunching that allows a horse sitting midfield to thread through and win with a sharp turn of foot.
scenarios.body: Lion's House is a true hold-up horse mapped to midfield due to redistribution and is therefore racing out of natural role, significantly reducing confidence in this shape materialising cleanly. Even if the field concertinas, Lion's House has zero wins from 15 runs on good going and an OR of only 66, meaning even the most favourable scenario carries limited conviction.

watchPoints.text: Thornaby Pearl — if she clears Loleeta in the opening furlong and gets a soft lead, her recent form and going figures make her genuinely difficult to peg back over 5f.

Loleeta's 87-day absence — watch her market moves; if she drifts significantly pre-race it will confirm she is not at peak fitness and the pace duel may be less intense than anticipated, benefiting hold-up types.

Merrimack's draw and early positioning — as a prominent racer in a field where the two front-runners will fight for the rail, if he is caught wide early he may spend more energy than ideal before the race reaches its critical final two furlongs.

Lion's House trading behaviour — given his redistribution out of natural role and zero wins on good going, any significant market support would be an anomaly worth noting but his tactical disadvantage in this field shape remains clear.

Going correction at race time — the going report lists this race as Good To Firm despite the declared going of Good; any further drying out on the July course straight will place an even greater premium on early speed and prominent racing, further compressing the late-closer option.

races.name: William Hill Price Boosts Apprentice Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Prince Quattro
runners_data.note: Consistent seven-year-old with excellent course form over similar trips on Good ground, including a win over 16f on Good recently; operates as a hold-up horse but his record at Newmarket in this going band (2 wins, 2 places from 15 runs on similar) makes him credible if the pace unfolds to suit a finishing run.|
runners_data.comment: Prince Quattro arrives here on the back of a win last time out, handles today's trip and conditions, and his rating of 72 suggests he holds strong claims as the second-ranked runner in the field; the main risk is whether 142 lb blunts that momentum.

runners_data.name: Jack Langley
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner and sole pace influence in this race, giving him total control of the tempo on the July course's flat 1m6f track; his trainer has only one winner from six in the 14-day window and he steps up sharply in trip, but being able to dictate entirely is a significant positional advantage regardless.|
runners_data.comment: Jack Langley shaped with plenty of promise last time, finishing second, and he was a winner the start before that — his experience over today's trip and going bolsters his claims at 141 lb; the main risk is whether 35 days off has left him short of peak sharpness.

runners_data.name: Baltic
runners_data.note: Consistent on Good ground over 14f-16f trips with a win at that distance in similar conditions; wears a tongue-tie and is freshened up after just 11 days — one of the closer-tracking types who could naturally sit just behind Langley in a small field, a position that suits given the sparse competition for places.|
runners_data.comment: Baltic shaped well when second last time out and has experience of today's trip and conditions, leaving him well placed on that score. Winless in his last five starts, but our rating still has him on top and he looks the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Stitching Wheel
runners_data.note: Holds genuine form credentials over 14f-16f on Good ground including a win and multiple places at similar trips, but is a true hold-up type whose deepest asset is a late run; in a race where the pace is calm and controlled, that style is structurally compromised — factor in the style-fit discount when weighing its prospects.|
runners_data.comment: Runner-up latest and a winner two starts back in recent form, Stitching Wheel faces a stiff ask ranked fifth of six on our figures, and a hefty 130 lb isn't helping; she has run over today's trip and going before, and a win two starts back shows she can find the line.

runners_data.name: Dereham
runners_data.note: A seasoned ten-year-old who has shown consistent form around 16f on Good ground, placing multiple times in this going band with a solid record of being competitive; naturally settles at the rear of the field, meaning the tempo needs to be strong enough to tire the leader before this one's late effort can land.|
runners_data.comment: Placed third last time out and showing consistent placed form in recent starts, Dereham has run over today's trip and going and carries a workable 127 lb; the pulled-up run three starts back is the one caution flag for a gelding yet to score in this sequence.

runners_data.name: Fram Castle
runners_data.note: Wears a visor and drops significantly in class to OR 53, but course form over 16f on Good ground includes a recent second in that band — naturally a hold-up horse in terms of racing style, and at 17 days since last run he arrives reasonably fresh; the style-fit note tempers confidence in a scenario where he cannot get his natural position.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked last on our figures, Fram Castle faces a stiff task here; a second last time out offers some encouragement, and he has run over today's trip and going before, but he must overturn a significant ratings gap to trouble the principles.

races.paceDynamic: Jack Langley is the sole confirmed front-runner in a six-runner field over 1m6f on Good to Firm ground at Newmarket's July course, and with no genuine challenger for the lead he can dictate a controlled, measured gallop from the front without being pressured at any stage. That uncontested, sustainable tempo suits a horse who can organise himself up front and conserve energy through the long flat straight, making this a classically shaped race where the pace is fair but not punishing. The five hold-up horses — Prince Quattro, Baltic, Stitching Wheel, Dereham, and Fram Castle — will be forced to track from behind, and with no secondary pace to quicken things up in the middle stages, closers relying on a truly strong gallop to bring them into contention may be left wanting. This race shape heavily favours a well-placed prominent racer or a hold-up horse with elite finishing speed over this trip; the field contains more true hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear, and those most likely to secure a forward position behind Jack Langley are Prince Quattro, with his course-proven finishing record, and Baltic, who can travel strongly in a small field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Langley Dictates Alone
scenarios.trigger: If Jack Langley leads throughout at a controlled Good to Firm pace and no rival applies early pressure, setting a gallop he entirely commands.
scenarios.body: Langley rolls along uncontested, conserving energy through the middle of the race and quickening modestly in the straight before hold-up horses can organise a serious challenge; horses closest to him at the two-furlong marker are best placed to capitalise on any late fade.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fast enough to stretch the field and a hold-up horse produces a sustained late run from off the bridle.
scenarios.body: With a small field and uncontested pace, a resolute stayer operating over a genuinely suitable trip on this going can pick off a tiring leader in the final furlong; the key is having enough early pace to create separation that the closer can reel in.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If a horse tracks Langley just off the pace throughout and pounces when Langley inevitably tires on this long flat trip.
scenarios.body: A hold-up horse who travels kindly in the first-rank of the chasing group — effectively acting as a prominent racer in this small field — can benefit the moment the leader's stride shortens; the flat Newmarket straight gives a long, measured run-in that rewards those who time their move well.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Shock Result — Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If Langley goes off too fast for himself or the race implodes tactically and a longer-priced stayer at a big price grinds to the front.
scenarios.body: An unexpected collapse in the leader's stamina or a mid-race tactical shake-up could hand a shock result to a consistent staying type at the bottom of the weights who has been quietly progressive; this is a low-probability scenario given the controlled expected tempo.

watchPoints.text: Jack Langley's ability to control tempo entirely is the defining race shape factor — watch whether he is allowed to coast in front or if any rival makes an unexpected move to his shoulder in the first half mile, as that alone could transform the outcome.

Prince Quattro's recent Good-ground win over 16f and strong course record (2W from 15 on similar going) make him the most likely beneficiary if the pace eases sufficiently to allow a hold-up horse to produce a finishing burst in the straight.

Baltic has shown ability on Good ground over staying trips and, in a small field, could find himself naturally tracking Langley rather than operating as a true closer — watch for Ashley Lewis positioning him closer than his style rating implies from an early stage.

Stitching Wheel and Dereham are both genuine hold-up types that have been mapped to midfield due to redistribution — if the pace is genuinely modest, these two may not get the searching gallop their style demands and could find themselves flattering to deceive at the business end.
